scope: Hosting and architecture sizing for W9 (hosting-and-architecture): data sizes, the address-to-cell join, hosting limits and costs, and three architectures. Research only. Nothing committed or pushed; only this JSON was written in the repository.
method: Downloads and derived files sit under scratchpad/hail-dl/hosting-and-architecture (folders s3-lists, derived, web, msl-structures, grib-sample, crops). Steps: HEAD of every 12:00 UTC file in the window; listings of June 15 folders and one 1440-minute day folder; a stratified sample of 115 daily files (summer 81, shoulder 24, winter 10, drawn with a fixed seed) decoded with eccodes and cropped to the Montana outline mask; stratified expansion to five years with 95% sampling intervals; a join of the MSL structure points to 0.01 degree cells and 0.1 degree tiles; page fetches of hosting terms and limits with phrase checks on the saved text. Read-only use of W1, W6, W7, p0-gates.json, the worktree basemap and workflow files.

limits: Sample-based estimates: 115 of 1,825 days, weighted by stratum. The 95% intervals cover sampling error only, not measurement error, unit error or code meaning. Summer is well sampled (81 of 459 days); shoulder and winter are thin (24 of 610; 10 of 756). Two days were added by hand (2025-06-15, 2025-06-16).

Units: GRIB units read 'unknown' in every file. Inch equivalents assume file values are mm; W1 and mrms.json record the unit as unverified. Values at 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 inch equivalents are conditional on that assumption.

Codes: -1 is treated as no event and -3 as no event; the meaning of -1, -3, -99 and -999 is unverified (NSSL table unreachable: HTTP 503 and TLS failures recorded in p0-gates.json and W1). Only positive file values are counted as events.
Positive MESH values are radar estimates, not observed hail or damage. The table counts cell-days with positive estimates; no report or inspection is implied.
The Montana outline is a simplified 2017 state boundary (basemap, from the us-atlas Census file); outline cell counts are approximate.

Parquet and vector tiles were not measured: pyarrow, DuckDB, tippecanoe and GDAL are not installed, and binary packages were not installed. A gzip columnar proxy (2.56 B per row) and a row-run proxy stand in.
Timings and throughput are from this environment (4 threads, 2.22 MB/s); GitHub-hosted runners were not tested.

Address points are the MSL Structures Framework (all structure types, 674,715). W6's housing-unit count (514,803) is inferred and unverified here; the Census API returned a missing-key page to W6 and no key was requested.
The 12:00 UTC file's 24-hour window is taken from W1, which reports an exact match to the 2-minute frames; not re-verified here.
Daily arrival: one observation (2025-06-16 12:00 file, Last-Modified 12:08:20 GMT). A schedule needs several days of observations.
Archive counts in the sample files are file values; no point report, storm report or damage record was matched here.
The existing site size was not measured (the site is built in CI); the estimates here cover only the hail additions.

architectures.name: A. Static shards only (GitHub Pages)
architectures.holds: Positive-cell events per 0.1 degree tile (gzip JSON), address-to-cell pointers, address index per tile; daily update adds one 12:00 file's rows.
architectures.bytes: events 32,584,386 B (interval 23,787,741 to 41,381,031); join pointers 1,343,386 B; address index about 5,606,882 B (W7 rate). Total about 39.5 MB, 4.0% of the 1 GB published limit (computed). Dense daily grid alternative: 18,766,062 B.
architectures.monthly_cost: No charge stated for Pages on the limits page read; public repository, so Actions minutes are free. Soft limits: 100 GB per month bandwidth.
architectures.per_lookup: Median tile about 6,592 B (events 1,842 rows x 3.52 B, plus 12 addresses x 8.31 B); p99 tile about 48,799 B; largest tile (33,855 addresses) about 310,433 B. Lookups before the 100 GB soft limit: about 15.2 million (median), 2.05 million (p99), 0.32 million (largest tile). Computed, not a traffic forecast.
architectures.can_answer: Five-year count of positive MESH cell-days (radar estimate) for each 0.01 degree cell and 0.1 degree tile, for addresses already in the index; daily refresh from a daily build.
architectures.cannot_answer: Wind (no wind data in this sizing); warnings (W3); point reports (W2); a free-text address that is not in the index (needs a geocoder, W7); anything newer than the last build.
architectures.rule_or_decision: Fits the current site rule (the browser fetches only site files). Build must not commit shards to main (repository size guidance). The 10-minute build (15-minute job timeout) cannot carry the backfill; only the daily update belongs in it.
architectures.risk: Counsel questions on publishing through Actions and Pages (terms section). Largest tile is 33,855 addresses, so the index may need splitting. Scheduled runs are unreliable (about 9.5 a day observed; dropped at top-of-hour load): the daily job needs a retry and a manual trigger.

architectures.name: B. Static site plus object storage (Cloudflare R2)
architectures.holds: Site files as in A; the raw 12:00 UTC archive (0.90 GB) or shards in R2 for re-derivation and future data.
architectures.bytes: Raw archive 901,938,706 B fits the 10 GB-month free storage (computed). 2-minute archive about 69.1 GB would be 59.1 GB above the free tier.
architectures.monthly_cost: $0 at this scale: daily writes of 4,597 tile objects = 137,910 Class A per month (free 1,000,000). The 2-minute archive would cost about $0.89 per month for storage, plus about $1.42 one-time for 1,314,720 Class A writes if loaded in one month (computed from R2 prices).
architectures.per_lookup: Same bytes as A, fetched from R2 (one Class B read per tile; 10 million free per month). Egress is free.
architectures.can_answer: Everything in A, plus re-derivation from the raw archive and storage of 2-minute frames if a product needs them.
architectures.cannot_answer: Same limits as A. Adds an off-site host to the browser path.
architectures.rule_or_decision: Blocked by the current site rule (the browser fetches only site files) unless the owner accepts an off-site host (D32 is pending in the brief).
architectures.risk: Off-site fetches; R2 storage is Standard class only for the free tier.

architectures.name: C. Small service with a database (Cloudflare Workers and D1)
architectures.holds: Events table in D1 (cell, day, value) and an address table; a Worker answers lookups.
architectures.bytes: Events as 8 bytes per positive row before indexes: 73,961,360 B (74 MB) against the 500 MB free database limit (index overhead not measured). Address table not measured.
architectures.monthly_cost: $0 on the free plans at this scale, with limits: Workers 100,000 requests per day; D1 5 million rows read per day (about 294,118 median-cell lookups per day). Peak sampled day (2022-07-09) had 133,429 positive rows, above the 100,000 free rows written per day, so daily writes need batching or the 0.25 in table (53,081 rows that day). Paid plan: $5 USD per month minimum.
architectures.per_lookup: Typical cell reads about 17.0 rows (median estimate); Workers Free CPU limit 10 ms per request (text found: True).
architectures.can_answer: Arbitrary point or address queries with server-side logic; new data without rebuilding the site; per-request filtering.
architectures.cannot_answer: Works without a server only in A and B; C needs a running service (uptime, updates, abuse controls).
architectures.rule_or_decision: Breaks the static-site rule in AGENTS.md (Python builds all pages) and the browser-fetches-site-files rule; needs a new decision.
architectures.risk: Free-plan write cap on peak days; per-request CPU budget; database size limit. A backfill of about 9.25 M positive rows takes about 93 days of Free-plan writes.
